#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  tsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    # glibc's tzset locks what TSan cannot see: see tsan.supp.
    export TSAN_OPTIONS=${TSAN_OPTIONS:-halt_on_error=1:suppressions=$here/crustify/scripts/tsan.supp}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" -Zbuild-std --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  bsan)
    # trybuild's nested cargo build does not finish under BorrowSanitizer, and the
    # compile-fail suite is a compile-time check the plain variant already runs.
    # Under parallel test threads BorrowSanitizer's GC can take longer than its default
    # 10 s hang threshold to bring every thread to a safepoint, and then aborts; give it
    # 120 s rather than serialize the tests.
    export BSAN_OPTIONS=${BSAN_OPTIONS:-gc_hang_threshold_ms=120000}
    if [ "${1:-}" = test ]; then
      case " $* " in
        *" -- "*) exec cargo bsan "$@" --skip compile_fail ;;
        *) exec cargo bsan "$@" -- --skip compile_fail ;;
      esac
    fi
    exec cargo bsan "$@" ;;
  *)
    echo "unknown variant: $variant" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

content.content:
## 4. Landing

A batch lands its commits on the integration branch it was given, which is never checked
out. Before committing, the diff is checked to contain no unrelated work. A commit carries
no trailer but the co-author trailers of the campaign's [identity](#6-identity), and its
subject says what it does and which run made it. A batch's names its module's file and its
objective and ends with its run's id, as `refs.c: wrap 12 items (wave-3/batch-1/run-2)`,
and its body lists the items it translated by their anchors' paths, as
`fn::git_reference_lookup`, one per line; a review batch's two commits name what they file
and what they fix the same way, and a planner run's subject ends with its run's id. A
progress commit is `progress: wave-<index>`, and an integration's merge, in the campaign's
repository and on the fork's `main`, `integrate <module>`, the module written as
[`modules-schema`](../../artifacts/modules-schema/SKILL.md) writes it.

The landing operation is a local push of the batch's tip to the integration branch through
the repository's Git common directory, which accepts only a fast-forward. A direct ref
update is no substitute: its compare-and-swap form makes the update atomic, but does not
enforce that the new commit descends from the expected old commit.

### 4.1 The landing lock

An integration branch is landed on by one batch at a time, under its landing lock: an
exclusive `flock` on a file in the Git common directory, named after the branch with its
`refs/heads/` prefix dropped, so that every worktree of the repository sees the same lock:

```text
$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock
```

A batch whose validated work is committed on its own branch takes the lock and holds it
until its landing has succeeded:

1. it acquires the lock, waiting while another batch holds it;
2. it rebases only its own branch onto the current integration branch, once: nothing else
   lands while it holds the lock;
3. it resolves any conflict the rebase raises and runs again, on the rebased tree, the
   gates that could catch a regression of the integration, as
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section describes, fixing what fails;
4. it pushes the fast-forward, which nothing can reject; and
5. it releases the lock.

A conflict or a failing gate is resolved under the lock rather than after releasing it, so
that the branch cannot move again in between and no batch rebases twice.

The waiter blocks in `flock` itself, so the kernel wakes it the moment the lock is released,
and nothing polls. Once it holds the lock, it hands the locked descriptor to a process of
its own, detached from the shell that started it and bound to the lifetime of the agent's
CLI: a `flock` lock belongs to the open file, so that process keeps it after the command
that took it exits, until that CLI ends, however it ends, and the kernel releases it. The
holder records itself beside the lock, in `<integration branch>.lock.holder`, as its own pid
and the CLI's. A waiter bounds each wait, to stay within the time a single command may run,
and waits again when it expires. For example, with `$CLI_PID` the agent CLI's pid, found by
walking up the shell's parent processes:
<!-- TODO: this procedure must run exactly so: it belongs in a script beside this skill,
documented by its `--help`, as `authoring` describes. -->

```bash
lock="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lock")"
# wait in the kernel, up to 10 minutes per command; then hand the lock to a detached holder
sh -c '
  exec 9>"$1"
  flock -w 600 9 || exit 1
  setsid sh -c "echo \"\$\$ $2\" > \"$1.holder\"; exec tail --pid=$2 -f /dev/null" 9>&9 &
' sh "$lock" "$CLI_PID"
# release, once the push has succeeded
holder=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$lock.holder"); rm -f "$lock.holder"; kill "$holder"
```

The holder file is removed before the holder is ended, while the lock is still held, so
that a release never removes the next holder's record.

The lock has no timeout: the regression gates it covers vary in length. A holder that has
stopped making progress keeps it until its agent is ended. That releases it where the
agent ran in a CLI of its own. An agent that shared its CLI with others leaves its holder
running: the holder is then ended as a release ends it, by the pid its record names, the
record removed first. The batch is then run again, as any failed batch is.

### 4.2 Commits

Every landing is a fast-forward, so an integration branch is linear, and each batch's
commits are one unbroken run of it, ending at its branch's tip and starting after the wave
base or the tip of the batch that landed before it: the commits its branch reaches and
neither the wave base nor the wave's other landed batches reach, oldest first, which
become the batch's `commits` in `schedule.json`.

The integration branch is never reset, force-updated or moved backward, and nothing is
pushed to a remote. The worktree stays after landing, until it is purged as [Lifecycle](#5-lifecycle)
describes.
<!-- TODO: when the working and shipping branches, and a wrapper's, are pushed to their
remotes is not specified yet, though a wrapper's reuse and a Git-pinned dependency need
it. -->

### 4.3 Promotion

A wave that has landed every batch is promoted to the branch it forked from, the module's
branch or the working branch, by a fast-forward to its tip, with the same local push
through the Git common directory, which rejects anything but a fast-forward.

### 4.4 Progress

The progress recorded while waves run, in `schedule.json`, the dashboard's usage and
campaign cells, and the `status` of a module in `modules.json` that a wrap batch ahead of
its consumer freezes, is committed on the working branch whenever no module is integrating. No agent writes
`schedule.json`, and no module branch changes it.

### 4.5 Integration

A module's branch is integrated into the working branch once the
last wave of its run has been promoted to it. Other modules may have been integrated since
it forked, so the working branch is merged into it, in its worktree, rather than the
other way around: the module's commits keep their ids, which its batches' `commits`
record, and the working branch still moves only by fast-forward.

1. The working branch's tip is merged into the module's branch. The files every module
   adds to, the dashboard's rows, the raw bindings' allowlists, `src/lib.rs`'s module
   declarations and the safe crate's export features, conflict additively, and so does a
   module's file in which two runs homed different items ahead of their consumers, with
   the declarations of the modules on its path: each conflict
   keeps both sides, a file's items in one of each of its regions, and the generated bindings are regenerated from the merged input. Any other conflict is a defect of the integration, resolved without
   discarding either side. No merge is committed while its tree holds a conflict marker,
   here or wherever a branch takes another by merge, such as a wave's branch taking the
   working branch, so that every branch forked from it starts from a tree that builds.
2. The merge's tree passes the gates of
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section, and in
   a port campaign, in the run that holds the last wave of the module's `wrap` and `port`
   items, the module's switch from C to Rust, which happens once, as
   [`porting-workflow`](../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section describes:
   its export feature is deleted, and the C test cases none of its `unit_pub` tests carries
   over are listed before its C tests leave.
3. The working branch is fast-forwarded to the module's branch.

Modules integrate one at a time, and nothing else is committed on the working branch while
one does, so that its fast-forward cannot be rejected. A port's later-stage waves come after
their module's switch, are promoted to the working branch, and integrate nothing, as
the porting workflow's Later stages section describes.

## 5. Lifecycle

Each branch and worktree exists only while its part of the campaign needs it. Before a part starts, everything it is named for exists; once it is promoted, what
only it needed is purged.

### 5.1 Campaign

The working branch is created during setup, in the repository the campaign creates, with
the C under `c/` and `crustify/CRUSTIFY.md` in its first commit. The shipping branch is created at the same commit and stays there
until the user first approves shipping. Both last for the campaign.

The working branch is committed to only when nothing is being promoted or integrated to
it, so that every promotion and integration is a fast-forward: the progress recorded in
the meantime stays in the base checkout's working tree until then, as
[Progress](#44-progress) describes.

### 5.2 Planner runs

A planner run's branch is forked from the working branch's tip and checked out in the repository's base dir. Once the run has committed, the working
branch is checked out and fast-forwarded to it, and the next run forks from there.

### 5.3 Modules

A module's base is the working branch's commit that holds its scaffolded `.rs` file and
the settings it runs under, committed before its first wave.

A module's branch is forked from its base before its first wave,
once the waves of other modules that its waves depend on have been integrated. A module
whose waves the order splits, such as one that wraps a cut dependency ahead of its
consumer, or one whose wave waits for an item another module's run holds, as
[`scheduling`](../../planning/scheduling/SKILL.md)'s Wrap batches section describes, runs once per contiguous run of its waves, each run on a branch forked anew
from the working branch. In a port campaign, only the run that holds the last wave of the
module's `wrap` and `port` items switches it from C; an earlier run's integration merges
its Rust alone, the module still C. Once a run has been integrated, its branch and worktree
are purged; its end state is the working branch's commit its last run integrates into.

### 5.4 Waves

A wave's integration branch is forked from its module's branch's tip, or, for a port's
later-stage wave, which runs after its module's switch, from the working branch's tip,
before any of its batches launch, so that it exists before the first landing, as [Branches](#2-branches)
requires; that commit is the wave's base.
Once every batch has landed, the wave is promoted, as [Promotion](#43-promotion)
describes, and its branch purged.

A translation wave's review batches are batches of the wave itself, and it is promoted once
they have landed too. An audit's review waves fork as any wave does.

### 5.5 Batches

A batch's branch and worktree, forked from its wave branch's tip, are created before it
launches, with its run dir, as [`layout`](../layout/SKILL.md) describes. The gitignored state its tree needs and does
not build itself, such as shared analysis databases, is symlinked from the base checkout,
and its `c/` is a worktree of the base checkout's submodule at the commit the superproject
records, since no batch changes the C.
Once the batch has landed, its worktree is purged; its branch stays until its commits are
recorded in `schedule.json`, since they are derived from it, as
[Landing](#4-landing) describes. A batch that fails keeps its branch and worktree for
inspection; they are removed before it is run again, which forks them anew.

## 6. Identity

A translation wave's review batches are batches of the wave itself, and it is promoted once
they have landed too. An audit's review waves fork as any wave does.

### 5.5 Batches

A batch's branch and worktree, forked from its wave branch's tip, are created before it
launches, with its run dir, as [`layout`](../layout/SKILL.md) describes. The gitignored state its tree needs and does
not build itself, such as shared analysis databases, is symlinked from the base checkout,
and its `c/` is a worktree of the base checkout's submodule at the commit the superproject
records, since no batch changes the C.
Once the batch has landed, its worktree is purged; its branch stays until its commits are
recorded in `schedule.json`, since they are derived from it, as
[Landing](#4-landing) describes. A batch that fails keeps its branch and worktree for
inspection; they are removed before it is run again, which forks them anew.

description: "The dashboard, its cells, the runs' records and transcripts, and how cost and time are derived. Read before filling dashboard cells or collecting a run's records."
---

# Accounting

What a campaign records about its own work: the dashboard, the runs' records and
transcripts its figures come from, and how cost and time are derived from them.

## 1. The dashboard

The dashboard, `crustify/artifacts/dashboard.md` unless the settings name another, is the
campaign's record of what each planner run, batch, wave and module did and cost. It is
filled from `templates/translate/dashboard.template.md`, an audit's from
`templates/audit/dashboard.template.md`, and keeps the template's format exactly.
When an adopted Crustify change adds a table or a column to the template, it is
added to the dashboard on the working branch before the next batch launches: a batch
fills the rows of the tables in place, and never adds one.

It is tracked in the campaign's tree, so every agent's worktree holds a copy, and it is
filled as the work lands rather than at the end. Each figure is measured once, where it is
produced: no suite or scan is rerun only to record one.

## 2. Cells

The dashboard's cells fall into three kinds, by when their figures can be known.

### 2.1 Landing cells

The cells measured on the tree a landing commits:

- for a batch, under the route its items' `kind` selects, as
  [`task-schema`](../../artifacts/task-schema/SKILL.md)'s Routes section gives it: its rows
  in that route's `Batches`, tests, `Batches: safety audit` and `Batches: API stability` tables, and for a review batch in
  `Batches — review: PoC + reports`, each placed in module, wave and batch order under
  its `pass`, and for a module pass, which spans both routes, in `Module passes`; those
  tables' `Σ` rows; and the `Coverage stats` table and the Overview's LoC
  line;
- for a planner run, its row in `Planning`, but for its usage cells.

They are filled in the landing's last commit, and measured against the integration branch
tip it was rebased onto: coverage as [`testing-builds`](../../verification/testing/builds/SKILL.md)'s Coverage section measures
it, the safety audit columns as the changes in the dashboard's Safety audit metrics, and
the API stability columns as the changes to the API of the landing's items are classified. A
rebase that conflicts in the dashboard keeps every row both sides added, and the landing's
cells, `Σ` rows included, are measured again where the gates its rebase reruns cover them;
the others stand as measured on the batch's base.

An integration merge, and any merge of one branch into another, keeps every row both
sides added, and settles the rest so: an additive `Σ` cell is the sum over the merged
rows, ours plus theirs less the merge base's, and so are the Overview's `Rust LoC`
figures; a usage `Σ` cell, its per-unit cells included, sums only the rows that carry
usage, so that it is filled again with theirs; a coverage `Σ` cell, and the Overview's
`C LoC`, are the later landing's; and `Coverage stats` takes the merged suites' counts,
with the later landing's percentages until a gate measures the merged tree, which the
merge commit's message says. A table or section the template holds once is kept once,
with the rows of every copy, whether or not the merge conflicts there, and the merged
dashboard is checked for repeated headings before it is committed.

### 2.2 Usage cells

The cells known only once an agent has ended, from its usage: its cost, tokens and wall,
the per-unit costs derived from them, and their `Σ` cells. A batch's are filled on the
working branch once its row is there, once its module is integrated, as
[`versioning`](../versioning/SKILL.md) describes, or, for a port's later-stage batch, which
runs after its module's switch, once its wave is promoted. A planner run's are filled once the run is
promoted. A batch run more than once costs the sum of its runs.

### 2.3 Campaign cells

The cells that span agents: the `Module stats` table, the Overview's branch line and
test baseline, and the `Settings` lines. A module's row and the branch line are filled
when the module is integrated, and a port's module row again as each of its later-stage
waves is promoted, the baseline once it is recorded, and the `Settings` lines,
with a Notes entry, whenever a settings change is applied.

### 2.4 Side campaign cells

A side campaign keeps its own dashboard, in its own repository, and its figures are
measured there. The parent's `Side campaigns` table copies them, one row per wrapper, as
they stand at the commit the parent pins, and the `side campaigns` row of `Module stats`
sums the rows, so that the parent's `Σ campaign` covers what its side campaigns cost. A
wrapper's row is filled each time the parent's pin moves, and its `shipped at` cell when
the wrapper ships the commit the parent pins. A side campaign that serves several parents
appears in each, with the figures as of each one's pin.

An audit's dashboard follows the same kinds over its own tables.

## 3. Records

Every run's `task.json` records how its agent ran: its backend, billing, model proxy and
the arguments its CLI was given, and, once it starts, its `session_id`, which ties the run
to its session. The session's transcript, which its CLI keeps by session id, is the
agent's full log and the source of its accounting. An agent spawned as a subagent of
another session has no session of its own: its session id is `agent-<agent id>`, the
name its host gives its transcript, under the spawning session's `subagents/`.

A transcript is copied into crustify's home, as `transcripts/<session id>.jsonl`, as soon
as its agent ends, because the CLIs move and prune their own files. Its usage is derived
from the copy, as [`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) describes, with the backend and model proxy its
`task.json` names.

An evolution review is a run like any other: its `task.json` sits in its artifact dir, and
its transcript is collected and priced the same way, its cost counted with the sessions that
orchestrate the campaign and recorded, with its tokens and wall time, in its proposal's
Review section, so that what each review bought can be weighed against its cost.

The sessions that orchestrate the campaign are collected the same way: at the start of each session, the
transcripts of the sessions before it. A resumed session keeps its id while its transcript
grows: its transcript is copied again after each run, replacing the earlier copy. The
records, transcripts and rates stay in crustify's home.

## 4. Cost and time

A run's cost and tokens are its usage's `total.cost_usd` and `total.tokens`, as
[`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) derives them from its transcript. The computed cost is used, never a provider-reported
dollar total; under subscription billing it is the API-equivalent cost.

An agent's wall time is its usage's interval. A wave's runs from its first batch's
launch through its final review and regression gates, a review wave's in an audit through
its landing, and a module's from its first launch through its final gate.

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

content.content:
---
name: ffimap
description: "Deterministic counts and sites of a Rust crate's unsafe and FFI surface. Read before a batch lands (its safe-boundary scan and safety-audit cells), before planning an audit's worksets, and when reviewing for unsafety, contracts or UB."
---

# ffimap

ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over
HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and
visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree
agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before
its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them.

It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> > <file>.json
```

Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and
its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from
the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`,
`as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs
`from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C
value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on
ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> --ffibox --sys-crates <the -sys crates> --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \
    --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \
    > <file>.json
```

In a port campaign, a scan names with `--features` the export feature of every module not
yet switched, as the [conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Export features section
names them, so that the `ffi_export` gateways compiled under them are counted. Every scan
names the module's unsafe regions, as the conventions' Unsafe regions section names them,
with `--regions`.

Two scans are compared only when they name the same seams, regions and features.

Its counters form one tree, each named by its dotted path into the scan's `counts`, as
ffimap's `docs/schema.md` describes; a metric is a counter, or a combination of counters
that schema allows: a partition's leaves summed, a share read against the record it cuts,
or subtracted from it. `--sites <counter> ...` also lists where each named counter's
increments are, and takes leaves only, such as `fn.unsafe.pub`; the workspace is named
before it. The counters that recur:

- `fn.unsafe.pub`, the public `unsafe fn`s, the crate's public unsafe surface, of which
  `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.pub` are those neither a trait nor a seam required; and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, the raw pointers in
  their signatures;
- `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`, the
  raw pointers in public fields and in the signatures of public safe fns, together
  `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub`, the raw pointers on the safe public interface; and their
  `of_which.void` shares, the type-erased ones among them;
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, the references to a cell, less their
  `of_which.self_in_ref_accessor` and `of_which.self_in_trait_impl` shares, the positions
  ffibox sanctions: references to C memory where a handle belongs, which assert `noalias`,
  `readonly` or validity over memory C may write; `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std`, the same
  of the raw C structs; and `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`, the borrows,
  slices and strings formed from a raw pointer, over bytes C must neither free nor change
  while they live;
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`,
  each an unchecked assertion that a value may move to or be shared with another thread;
- `raw_ptr.deref.wr` and `raw_ptr.deref.rd`, raw-pointer writes and reads, each a pointer
  the implementer vouches is non-null, aligned, live, initialized and unaliased by a live
  reference; and
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` and
  `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`, the types that hold a raw pointer and
  tear it down or copy it by hand, and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}`, those
  that declare nothing about it. Each of these five also has a `.total`, the sum of its two
  leaves, which is no leaf for `--sites`.

ffimap is neither complete nor sound: its sites are where review starts, not all it
covers. It does not count the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, such as a reference
or lifetime-annotated handle made from a raw pointer by `&*p`, `from_ptr`, `from_raw` or
`from_raw_parts`, or changed by a `transmute`: those are found in the source.

What follows is how ffimap serves each stage: each section names the skill and section it
adds to, and states only what ffimap adds there.

## Binding and porting

### Binding › Safe boundary

Before a batch lands, a scan with `--sites fn.unsafe.pub raw_ptr.field.pub
raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub` lists the public
`unsafe fn`s and the raw pointers on the safe public interface, and each of those sites
that belongs to the batch's changeset and that a safe variant could replace is fixed.
Its `--sites` also name the unsafe code outside both regions,
`code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions`, another crate's macro expansions included,
which the `unsafe_code` lint misses, and `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.pub` and
`.priv`: outside the raw bindings, each of those sites in the batch's changeset is moved
into its region.

## Accounting

### Accounting › Landing cells

A batch's row in the dashboard's `Batches: safety audit` table is the change in each of
the Safety audit's metrics, from a scan of the tip its landing rebased onto to a scan of
the tree it lands.

### Accounting › API stability

`ffimap api` measures a safe crate's consumer-facing API per C item, from rustdoc JSON, as
its `docs/api.md` describes, read in full before its first use. A C item is the
`<kind>::<path>` of a `Wraps` or `Replaces` anchor, its surface every stand-in the anchor
names and the handles and owners tied to it, each judged by the contract
[`binding-types`](../../rust/binding/types/SKILL.md)' Safe layout section gives a consumer:
the methods every form offers, its reborrows and dereferences, and the traits a consumer
can use, never a form's raw access or seams. A batch generates the safe crate's rustdoc
JSON on the tip its landing rebased onto and on the tree it lands, with a nightly whose
`format_version` the tool supports, and ffibox's, with private items, for the contracts of
the forms it defines:

```bash
cargo +<nightly> rustdoc -p <crate> --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
ffimap api diff <base>.json <tree>.json --dep <ffibox>.json --items "<the worklist's keys>" --format json
```

Each item comes out `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed` or `new`, with its anchor's
move from `Wraps` to `Replaces` where a port made it. The batch's row in the dashboard's
`Batches: API stability` table counts them over its worklist, and over the crate's
unattributed public items, compared per module.

### Accounting › Records

An unseeded scan of the unsafe and FFI surface is recorded at each batch's, wave's and
the campaign's end, as `ffimap.json` in its artifact directory: a batch's in the run dir
of the run that landed it, a wave's in its wave's dir, as `layout` spells it, and the
campaign's in `crustify/artifacts/`. A module's end is the scan of the last wave of its `wrap` and `port` items.

## Reviewing

### Reviewing › Objectives

A review locates the sites of its objectives with a scan, `--sites` with their counters,
and keeps those in its workset: the code its commits add or change, or its modules and
the types, trait impls and functions they name.

- `unsafety`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`.
- `contracts`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, whose `# Safety` obligations are evaluated.
- `ub`: these smells first, in this order:
  1. references into C memory: the references to a cell outside its sanctioned positions,
     `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` less those shares, and to a raw C
     struct, `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, then
     `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`;
  2. thread-safety claims, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and
     `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`, checked against
     the C library's contract: a data race is reachable from safe code when the library
     does not allow what they assert;
  3. the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, found in the source: unsound when the
     handle can outlive the owner of the memory or the point at which C frees or
     invalidates it;
  4. raw pointers a consumer can set, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
     `raw_ptr.field.pub`, with their `of_which.void` shares: unsound when a safe path
     dereferences or frees what the consumer passed or stored;
  5. raw-pointer dereferences, `raw_ptr.deref.wr` then `raw_ptr.deref.rd`: first in the
     modules that also hold references into C memory, where a write may invalidate a
     reference, and outside a type's accessors; and
  6. hand-written teardown and copies, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}`
     and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`.

## Audit

### Audit workflow › Worksets

The audit's worksets are planned from a scan of the crate, run once each build
configuration it audits is in place, with `--sites` over the counters of its objectives.
A file outside every configuration scanned has no sites, and is planned from its source.

For `ub`, the modules that hold the smells ffimap's review guidance lists for `ub` are
reviewed first, in that order; for `contracts`, those that hold the crate's unsafe API and
its justifications, the `contracts` counters above. The rest of the crate
follows the smells.

The modules are batched by their sites, and a module that is split keeps a type, trait
impl or function with its sites in one batch. A site of `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop`,
`.impl_clone`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send` or `.sync`, at either leaf, is a trait impl, named
`Drop for <type>`, `Clone for <type>`, `Send for <type>` or `Sync for <type>`. Each review
runs the same scan over its own modules, so the sites are not passed on.

its `docs/api.md` describes, read in full before its first use. A C item is the
`<kind>::<path>` of a `Wraps` or `Replaces` anchor, its surface every stand-in the anchor
names and the handles and owners tied to it, each judged by the contract
[`binding-types`](../../rust/binding/types/SKILL.md)' Safe layout section gives a consumer:
the methods every form offers, its reborrows and dereferences, and the traits a consumer
can use, never a form's raw access or seams. A batch generates the safe crate's rustdoc
JSON on the tip its landing rebased onto and on the tree it lands, with a nightly whose
`format_version` the tool supports, and ffibox's, with private items, for the contracts of
the forms it defines:

```bash
cargo +<nightly> rustdoc -p <crate> --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
ffimap api diff <base>.json <tree>.json --dep <ffibox>.json --items "<the worklist's keys>" --format json
```

Each item comes out `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed` or `new`, with its anchor's
move from `Wraps` to `Replaces` where a port made it. The batch's row in the dashboard's
`Batches: API stability` table counts them over its worklist, and over the crate's
unattributed public items, compared per module.

### Accounting › Records

An unseeded scan of the unsafe and FFI surface is recorded at each batch's, wave's and
the campaign's end, as `ffimap.json` in its artifact directory: a batch's in the run dir
of the run that landed it, a wave's in its wave's dir, as `layout` spells it, and the
campaign's in `crustify/artifacts/`. A module's end is the scan of the last wave of its `wrap` and `port` items.

## Reviewing

### Reviewing › Objectives

A review locates the sites of its objectives with a scan, `--sites` with their counters,
and keeps those in its workset: the code its commits add or change, or its modules and
the types, trait impls and functions they name.

- `unsafety`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`.
- `contracts`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, whose `# Safety` obligations are evaluated.
- `ub`: these smells first, in this order:
  1. references into C memory: the references to a cell outside its sanctioned positions,
     `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` less those shares, and to a raw C
     struct, `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, then
     `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`;
  2. thread-safety claims, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and
     `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`, checked against
     the C library's contract: a data race is reachable from safe code when the library
     does not allow what they assert;
  3. the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, found in the source: unsound when the
     handle can outlive the owner of the memory or the point at which C frees or
     invalidates it;
  4. raw pointers a consumer can set, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
     `raw_ptr.field.pub`, with their `of_which.void` shares: unsound when a safe path
     dereferences or frees what the consumer passed or stored;
  5. raw-pointer dereferences, `raw_ptr.deref.wr` then `raw_ptr.deref.rd`: first in the
     modules that also hold references into C memory, where a write may invalidate a
     reference, and outside a type's accessors; and
  6. hand-written teardown and copies, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}`
     and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`.

## Audit

### Audit workflow › Worksets

The audit's worksets are planned from a scan of the crate, run once each build
configuration it audits is in place, with `--sites` over the counters of its objectives.
A file outside every configuration scanned has no sites, and is planned from its source.

For `ub`, the modules that hold the smells ffimap's review guidance lists for `ub` are
reviewed first, in that order; for `contracts`, those that hold the crate's unsafe API and
its justifications, the `contracts` counters above. The rest of the crate
follows the smells.

The modules are batched by their sites, and a module that is split keeps a type, trait
impl or function with its sites in one batch. A site of `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop`,
`.impl_clone`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send` or `.sync`, at either leaf, is a trait impl, named
`Drop for <type>`, `Clone for <type>`, `Send for <type>` or `Sync for <type>`. Each review
runs the same scan over its own modules, so the sites are not passed on.

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

# A compile-fail doctest's error code is checked only on nightly

Status: `open`: no change made. The destination is the `testing` skill, which the binder
does not evolve.

## Signal

A check the gates appear to run and do not. A wrong expectation passed a batch's gates.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-2/run-1` added seven `compile_fail` doctests to `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`.
One was first written `compile_fail,E0499`, for assigning to an argument array a `Parser`
borrows. The plain gate, on the pinned stable (Rust 1.100.0), passed it. Rewritten as
`compile_fail,E0000`, it passed again: stable rustdoc checks only that the snippet fails to
compile, never which error it fails with. Compiled with `rustc` against the built rlib, the
snippet reports `E0506` (cannot assign to `args[_]` because it is borrowed), which the batch
now expects. The codes of all seven were confirmed that way. Only a nightly rustdoc checks the
code, and the campaign runs nightly only in its sanitizer and Miri variants (Miri skips
doctests). There, the known `CommitBuilder` doctest (`src/libgit2/src/libgit2/commit.rs`,
`E0624`) is the one recorded failure. So a wrong code a batch writes is caught, if at all, at a
later gate, as a known nightly failure.

## Destination

The spec: `testing`'s UB tests section, beside "When the type system should reject a
program, the test is a compile-fail doctest or a `trybuild` case". It could say that a
doctest's error code is verified on the pinned nightly (`cargo +<nightly> test --doc`), or
each snippet compiled alone, since the stable gate does not check it. A `trybuild` case's
`.stderr` is checked on stable and needs no such step.

## Change

Not made: `testing` is not the binder's to evolve.

## Validation

The two stable runs above: `E0499` and `E0000` both passed `cargo test --doc` on 1.100.0, and
`rustc` reported `E0506`.

## Review

None yet.

# Adopting a handle over a layout type with a lifetime vouches for nothing about that lifetime

Status: `open`: no change made. The destination is ffibox, which a reviewer proposes changes
to and does not evolve.

## Signal

A contract that a caller can honour and still reach undefined behaviour (`reviewing`'s
`contracts` objective), stated once in ffibox and inherited by every layout type with a
lifetime: `define_ctype!`'s 3 uses with `phantom =` and the crate's 34 hand-written
`unsafe impl CCell for X<'_>`.

## Evidence

- `CCell::ref_from_ptr` (`src/traits.rs:907`), which `CRefSeam::from_ptr`,
  `CMutSeam::from_ptr`, their `void *` twins and `CCell::mut_from_ptr` forward to, asks only
  that "`ptr` must address a live, initialised `Self::C` (or be null) that outlives `'a`, and
  nothing may write it while the handle lives except through a `Mut` derived from the same
  borrow". `'a` is the handle's borrow. For `Self = Foo<'p>`, the getters of `FooRef<'a, 'p>`
  lend what the object points at for `'p`, and nothing in the contract says `'p` must hold.
  The caller names `'p`, `'static` included.
- `wave-186/batch-3`'s finding
  `contracts/ffi_import/adopted-handles-outlive-their-borrows`
  (`crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/batch-3/`): `SpecRef::<'_, 'static>::from_ptr`
  on a live `cli_opt_spec` keeps the stated contract word for word. `name()` then lends a
  `&'static CStr` that outlives its `CString`. Miri reports a dangling reference
  (`run-affected.log` there). opt.rs's getters justify their reads by "its handle's adoption",
  which no stated contract defines. The batch fixed it on its side, with an `# Adoption`
  section on each of `Spec`, `Opt` and `Parser` stating what an adopter vouches beyond the
  seams' contract.
- The same holds wherever a lifetime cell is adopted from a pointer: `Reference<'r>` (`refs.rs`),
  `Object<'r>`, `Blob<'r>` and the rest of `ffibox-lifetime-ctypes`' count. `Holder<'p>`'s
  example in `impl_cdrop!`'s rustdoc (`src/macros.rs`) writes the obligation into its own
  `SAFETY:` comment ("an owned holder whose parent outlives `'p`"), and `CBox::from_c` does
  too, but no `# Safety` section asks for it.

ffibox: the `# Safety` sections of `CCell::ref_from_ptr`, `mut_from_ptr`, `ref_from_void_ptr`
and `mut_from_void_ptr` (`src/traits.rs`), which the seams' `# Safety` sections cite, and of
the other adoptions of a `Self` value from a pointer (`CSlice::from_raw_parts`, `CBox::from_c`
and the owners' `from_raw`). Also the `define_ctype!` rustdoc's `phantom` paragraph, and
`docs/borrows.md`'s inbound-seam paragraph.

## Change

Add one clause to each of those contracts: the pointee is a valid `Self`, not only an
initialised `Self::C`. Every borrow the lifetimes of `Self` name lives for them, and every
invariant the type's safe operations rely on holds, as the type's own documentation states
it. Say in `define_ctype!`'s `phantom` paragraph that a type whose layout points at memory
it borrows documents that invariant, for its adopters, in an `# Adoption` section, as
opt.rs's `Spec`, `Opt` and `Parser` now do. The wording only makes explicit what the
existing `SAFETY:` examples already assume. No signature changes.

## Validation

Not made. The reproducer above fails under Miri at `fe6b85bfa`. With opt.rs's `# Adoption`
sections, the batch's `tests/ub_unsafe/src/cli/opt.rs` adopts each handle within the
extended contract, and Miri and ASan pass it.

## Review

None yet.
EOF

input.content:
# An adopted spec, outcome or parser lends its borrows for any lifetime its adopter names

- **finding**: `contracts/ffi_import/adopted-handles-outlive-their-borrows`
- **batch**: `wave-186/batch-3/run-1`, the review of `wave-186/batch-0` (`8a149ac08`) and
  `wave-186/batch-2` (`fe6b85bfa`), `opt.h`'s types
- **items**: `st::cli_opt_spec`, `st::cli_opt`, `st::cli_opt_parser`
- **affected commit**: `fe6b85bfa`
- **where**: `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, `mod ffi_import`: the handles `define_ctype!` mints
  for `Spec<'p>`, `Opt<'p>` and `Parser<'p>`, their public `unsafe` seams
  `CRefSeam::from_ptr` / `CMutSeam::from_ptr`, and the getters whose `SAFETY:` comments rest
  on "its handle's adoption": `SpecRef::{target, name, value_name, help}`,
  `OptRef::{spec, arg, value}`, `ParserRef::{specs, args}`, `ParserMut::args_mut` and
  `Arg::as_c_str`

## Finding

The three layouts carry `'p`, the lifetime of the strings, variables, spec table and
argument array they point at. Their getters lend those for `'p`, not for the handle's
borrow `'a`. For a handle built in Rust that is sound: each setter takes a `&'p` borrow.
For a handle adopted from a pointer, the getters' `SAFETY:` comments say "a spec C built
holds, by its handle's adoption, `NULL` or a string that lives unchanged for `'p`". No
contract asks an adopter for that. The only public adoption is ffibox's `CRefSeam::from_ptr`
and `CMutSeam::from_ptr`, whose `# Safety` is `CCell::ref_from_ptr`'s: "`ptr` must address a
live, initialised `Self::C` (or be null) that outlives `'a`, and nothing may write it while
the handle lives except through a `Mut` derived from the same borrow". It says nothing of
`'p`, which the adopter picks freely, nor of the `value` pointer matching its `type`, which
`target()` casts by. A caller who honours that contract still gets dangling borrows from
safe getters.

## Evidence

The reproducer, `src/main.rs` beside this report, builds a spec in Rust storage whose name
is a short-lived `CString`. It adopts the spec through `SpecRef::<'_, 'static>::from_ptr`,
keeping every clause of the stated contract: the spec is live and initialised, it outlives
the handle, and nothing writes it. It reads `name()`, a `&'static CStr`, then drops the spec
and the string. On `fe6b85bfa` Miri stops at the use (`run-affected.log`):

```
error: Undefined Behavior: constructing invalid value of type &std::ffi::CStr: encountered a dangling reference (use-after-free)
  --> src/main.rs:27:22
   |
27 |     println!("{:?}", name.to_bytes());
   |                      ^^^^ Undefined Behavior occurred here
```

The same holds for `OptRef::arg`, `OptRef::value` and `OptRef::spec`, and for
`ParserRef::specs` and `ParserRef::args`, which lend `'p` borrows read from the layout in
the same way.

## Reproducer

`Cargo.toml` and `src/main.rs` beside this report. From this directory, in a checkout of the
affected commit:

```
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=plain cargo +nightly-2026-10-08 miri run
```

It exits 1 with the report above. It calls no C, so Miri reaches it; an ASan build reports
the same use after free.

## Fix

The generic contract is ffibox's, so the general fix is proposed there:
`crustify/evolution/ffibox-adoption-of-lifetime-cells`. On the crate's side, `Spec`, `Opt`
and `Parser` each gain an `# Adoption` section stating what an adopter vouches beyond the
seams' contract: that the pointee is a valid `Spec<'p>`, `Opt<'p>` or `Parser<'p>` for the
`'p` it names. Its strings are `NULL` or NUL-terminated and live unchanged for `'p`. A spec's
`value` is `NULL` or a live variable of the type its `type` writes. An outcome's `spec`, and a
parser's table, are valid specs that live unchanged for `'p`, the table ended by a spec of
kind `CLI_OPT_TYPE_NONE`. A parser's arguments are `args_len` live non-null strings in an
array only the parser reaches. The getters' "by its handle's adoption" now refers to that
section. The reproducer adopts at `'static` a spec whose name lives shorter, so it no longer
honours the contract.

The regression test is `tests/ub_unsafe/src/cli/opt.rs`. It adopts each handle, shared and
exclusive, within the extended contract, then reads every getter and writes through the
exclusive ones. `an_adopted_spec_lends_its_strings_for_their_lifetime` is this scenario
adopted at its strings' lifetime. They pass plain, under ASan/UBSan and under Miri
(`run-fixed.log`).

content.content:
Tests: six `unit_pub` tests (the kinds a long name selects, the predicate in a `const` block,
`FORCE_GNU`, the default, unnamed flag bits, and `GNU` under `POSIXLY_CORRECT` unset, `1`, empty
and `0`, each in a child process of the test binary, since setting the environment is unsafe
beside the harness's threads), two `equiv` tests and two doctests. The equivalence of the macro
goes through `cli_opt_parser_next`, which parses `--opt` against every non-empty subset of the
seven listed kinds, in order and reversed, every spec named `opt`: the C's selected spec is the
first the Rust's predicate accepts, with the status that follows. That of the function goes
through `cli_opt_parser_init`'s `needs_sort`, for the four combinations of the style flags, each
beside none or three sets of unnamed bits, in three child environments. Mutating either port
(an accumulator as an option; `GNU` ignoring the variable) fails its equivalence test. The CLI
has no C tests to carry over. Worklist coverage: `opt.rs` 90 of 90 lines, 24 of 24 functions,
92 of 92 regions; C `support_gnu_style` every line, each branch reached, and the macro's line
of `spec_for_long` 224 times.

Coverage was measured with `crustify/scripts/coverage/run.sh` on this tree and read with
`report.py` from the scratch tree's `src/` (`C=@c` over the `coverage` variant's

content.content:
usage: ffimap [-h] [--sites COUNTER [COUNTER ...]]
              [--sys-crates CRATE[,CRATE...]] [--seams NAMES]
              [--regions NAMES] [--barriers NAMES]
              [--features FEATURE[,FEATURE...]] [--ffibox]
              WORKSPACE

Scan a Rust crate's unsafe surface and raw-pointer usage with a rustc driver
over HIR and typeck. Reproducible: same tree, same bytes. Needs the crate to
compile; when it does not, there are no counts rather than approximate ones.
It says HOW MUCH unsafety is there, never which of it is wrong.

positional arguments:
  WORKSPACE             Directory of the Cargo workspace (or package) to scan.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --sites COUNTER [COUNTER ...]
                        Also report where these counters' increments are in
                        the source: a `sites` record beside `counts` with one
                        list per counter. Takes a counter's dotted path down
                        to its LEAF (e.g. raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub,
                        ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub,
                        code.unsafe_call.ffi): a path that stops at an arm
                        above one validates and then reads empty, since the
                        driver emits by leaf. Line totals have no sites.
  --sys-crates CRATE[,CRATE...]
                        Crates whose #[repr(C)] types are C's: the crate's own
                        bindings and any other crate it reaches C through,
                        such as `libc`. The field walk descends through them
                        too, so a pointer a scanned type holds through one is
                        counted as the scanned crate's to manage. Nothing is
                        discovered: a Cargo `links` key and a `*-sys` name
                        both over-report, so unnamed means the peel set is the
                        scanned crate alone.
  --seams NAMES         Function names that are seams -- the conversion
                        between a wrapper and its raw pointer (`raw`,
                        `from_raw`, `as_ptr`, `from_ptr`). Newline- or comma-
                        separated, so `--seams "$(cat seams.txt)"` works. They
                        are counted as usual and ALSO reported as the
                        `of_which.seam` share of each fn-signature counter, so
                        a reader can tell plumbing from the pointer management
                        a consumer of the safe API actually faces. ffimap
                        never guesses the names.
  --regions NAMES       Module names that are regions -- the modules a crate

## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them
- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded
- `cost` / `review cost` / `total` — a module's translation, review and combined cost;
  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant
  out, `Σ campaign` adds it, without per-unit cells
- `UB safe tests` … `Unit tests` — `#[test]` functions per suite, each with the coverage of
  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and
  those with a `Replaces:` or a `Wraps:` anchor at the tip; `share` is of the total

Every table below is a heading, a model line and the table. All prose belongs
in Notes.

### Reading the batch tables

Batch rows from every sub-campaign share one table per route; the `module` cell names the
row's sub-campaign as `<link-unit>/<module>`, the same name as its Overview row.
Every type row is a `wrap` batch: the rows the wrap campaign landed, kept in the `Types`
tables' `objective` column since the template merged its wrap and port tables. A `wavefront` report category, for ownership findings the review resubmitted, is
counted under `+misc`.

Each batch is measured on two tree states: just before its first landing commit (the wave
base or the previous batch's landing) and its last landing commit. `cov (C/Rust)` is the
latter, from one instrumented build per state: the four workloads (`--lib` unit tests,
`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `equiv`) each run alone into their own profile directory against
the `coverage` prebuild, and their union is the cell. C is lcov line coverage over the 196
translation units `libgit2.so` links, with a zero baseline from the `.gcno` files so that
untouched TUs count; Rust is cargo-llvm-cov line coverage over `crustify/rust/libgit2`'s
non-`tests/` sources, minus every line inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (the inline unit-test
modules). All workloads share one denominator, and the union is the union of their covered
lines. Every Rust cell and Rust delta in these tables was restated on 2026-10-12. The
earlier figures counted those test lines, 60% of the instrumented lines at the
`libgit2/index` tip, which held the integration suites' coverage far down and credited
the unit tests for running themselves. All 182 recorded states were re-measured; the C
cells and C deltas stay as first recorded. The eight `libgit2/config` states between
`beeda6a07` and the export revert `c5440d3ee` call the two reverted constructors, so they
were measured against a private coverage build of their own source, which exports them. A Σ `cov` cell is the state after the table's chronologically
last landing. The `(+C/+Rust pp)` pairs in the `…: tests` tables are each workload's own
coverage after minus before, so a batch that adds code its workload does not reach shows a
negative Rust delta. The safety audit deltas are the Safety audit's metrics over the same two
states, from the scans the `ffimap` skill names; the tables hold no row from before the
metrics were redefined, as `Safety audit metrics from ffimap's counter tree` describes.

Test counts are `#[test]` functions the landing commits add, by directory; trybuild
`compile_fail` cases are not counted. `+LoC` and `rv loc` count `.rs` lines under
`crustify/rust/`, so review reproducer crates under `crustify/reviews/` are excluded. The
measurement scripts live outside the repository, beside the orchestrator's other helpers;
each batch's `ffimap.json` beside it is the unseeded scan of its last landing commit.

### Overview test counts

ergonomics/buf-confined-to-its-thread (st::reftable_buf)

The host refused the report file, so the report is in this message. The reproducer is
beside where it would be.

Buf is confined to the thread that made it, and its handle cannot be hashed. reftable's
buffer stands in for a Vec<u8> ("reftable_buf maps to Vec<u8>" in modules.json), and
ffibox's G1 asks for the standard traits of the counterpart, with each departure stated.
Two departures are neither stated nor needed:

1. define_ctype! withholds Send and Sync, and batches 0 (85ad07673) and 2 (2032628fd)
   wrote no proof. So Buf, BufVal, ReftableBox<Buf> and both handles stay on one thread.
   Nothing ties a buffer to its thread. Its allocation is reftable's, and the module's own
   Alloc contract requires every hook family to accept a cross-thread resize or release,
   which libgit2's and libc's allocators accept. The ReftableStr that BufMut::detach hands
   out, over the same allocation, already crosses threads (ub_safe's
   strings_and_runs_are_released_on_other_threads). Every operation a shared borrow
   reaches only reads.
2. BufRef is Eq and Ord by content (reftable_buf_cmp) but not Hash.

Reproducer: in crustify/reviews/foundational/libgit2/deps/reftable/basics.c/wave-169/
batch-3/ergonomics/buf-confined-to-its-thread, run
`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=plain cargo run`. It moves a filled BufVal to another thread,
which grows it; two threads then read it at once, and a third releases it. On bbaafcd09
it does not compile:

  error[E0277]: `*const ()` cannot be sent between threads safely
    --> src/main.rs:21:17
     = help: within `ffibox::refs::CVal<...::Buf, BufRelease>`, the trait `Send` is not
       implemented for `*const ()`
  note: required because it appears within the type `...::basics::Buf`
  error: could not compile `buf-confined-to-its-thread` ... due to 2 previous errors

The fix follows in the next commit, after which the reproducer exits 0.

ergonomics/buf-confined-to-its-thread (st::reftable_buf)

The host refused the report file, so the report is in this message. The reproducer is
beside where it would be.

Buf is confined to the thread that made it, and its handle cannot be hashed. reftable's
buffer stands in for a Vec<u8> ("reftable_buf maps to Vec<u8>" in modules.json), and
ffibox's G1 asks for the standard traits of the counterpart, with each departure stated.
Two departures are neither stated nor needed:

1. define_ctype! withholds Send and Sync, and batches 0 (85ad07673) and 2 (2032628fd)
   wrote no proof. So Buf, BufVal, ReftableBox<Buf> and both handles stay on one thread.
   Nothing ties a buffer to its thread. Its allocation is reftable's, and the module's own
   Alloc contract requires every hook family to accept a cross-thread resize or release,
   which libgit2's and libc's allocators accept. The ReftableStr that BufMut::detach hands
   out, over the same allocation, already crosses threads (ub_safe's
   strings_and_runs_are_released_on_other_threads). Every operation a shared borrow
   reaches only reads.
2. BufRef is Eq and Ord by content (reftable_buf_cmp) but not Hash.

Reproducer: in crustify/reviews/foundational/libgit2/deps/reftable/basics.c/wave-169/
batch-3/ergonomics/buf-confined-to-its-thread, run
`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=plain cargo run`. It moves a filled BufVal to another thread,
which grows it; two threads then read it at once, and a third releases it. On bbaafcd09
it does not compile:

  error[E0277]: `*const ()` cannot be sent between threads safely
    --> src/main.rs:21:17
     = help: within `ffibox::refs::CVal<...::Buf, BufRelease>`, the trait `Send` is not
       implemented for `*const ()`
  note: required because it appears within the type `...::basics::Buf`
  error: could not compile `buf-confined-to-its-thread` ... due to 2 previous errors

The fix follows in the next commit, after which the reproducer exits 0.

Spec, Opt and Parser each gain an # Adoption section. It states what a caller of
CRefSeam::from_ptr / CMutSeam::from_ptr vouches beyond those seams' contract: the pointee
is a valid layout for the 'p it names. Its strings live unchanged for 'p, a spec's value
is NULL or a variable of the type its kind writes, and a parser's table is ended and its
arguments are reached only through it. Five ub_unsafe tests (tests/ub_unsafe/src/cli/opt.rs,
a new module of the suite) adopt each handle, shared and exclusive, within that contract.
They pass plain, under ASan+UBSan and under Miri. The generic contract is ffibox's, filed as
crustify/evolution/ffibox-adoption-of-lifetime-cells.

Spec gains by-value builders: with_name, with_alias (0 for none, as C's '\0'),
with_switch_value, with_usage, with_value_name and with_help, each anchored to its field.
The module's equiv and ub_safe spec tables are declared with them. unit_pub's
builders_set_what_the_setters_set and a doctest cover them. API: the six fields' keys are
extended, and every other key of the worklist is kept.

The dashboard's landing cells and Notes entry, and the run's task.json, task.md,
ffimap.json and api-diff.json.

content.text:
The review of `wave-186/batch-3` is done and landed on `crustify/waves/wave-186`: `77e6925d8` files the reports and `3829c7a06` fixes them. I found two problems in the opt.c types and fixed both; the other objectives found nothing.

## Findings

**1. `contracts/ffi_import/adopted-handles-outlive-their-borrows`** (has a reproducer)
- **Problem:** a `Spec`, `Opt` or `Parser` handle can be built from a raw pointer through ffibox's public `CRefSeam::from_ptr` or `CMutSeam::from_ptr`. A caller can follow that function's stated contract exactly and still get dangling references. Nothing in the contract limits the lifetime `'p` the caller picks for what the struct points at.
- **Proof:** the reproducer picks `'static` and reads a spec's name after its string is freed. Miri reports a use-after-free. It calls no C.
- **Fix:** `Spec`, `Opt` and `Parser` each gain an `# Adoption` doc section saying what such a caller must also guarantee.
- **Regression tests:** five new tests in `tests/ub_unsafe/src/cli/opt.rs` build each handle this way within the full contract. They pass on plain, under ASan/UBSan and under Miri.

**2. `ergonomics/spec-built-one-setter-at-a-time`**
- **Problem:** building a spec took one `as_mut()` setter call per field, applied by index after the table existed. C writes one initialiser per spec.
- **Fix:** `Spec` gains chainable builders: `with_name`, `with_alias` (where `0` means no alias), `with_switch_value`, `with_usage`, `with_value_name` and `with_help`.
- **Callers:** the module's `equiv` and `ub_safe` tables now use them, and a new unit test plus a doctest cover them.
- **API stability:** the API diff counts the six builder fields as extended and the other 51 worklist items as kept.

The other objectives found nothing:
- **UB:** every borrow is tied to `'p` or the handle; the three structs are invariant in `'p`.
- **Unsafety:** no public raw pointer or `unsafe fn` in the workset.
- **Equivalence:** the enums' C values and the state `cli_opt_parser_init` sets up already match C.
- **Logic:** the documented effects match `opt.c`'s parse.
- **Idiom and conventions:** nothing in the workset.
- **Test adequacy:** `opt.rs` is at 562 of 563 lines. The remaining line is unreachable from safe code or C.

## Gates
- **Run:** formatting with the pinned nightly's rustfmt, and `clippy --all-targets --all-features` with warnings denied.
- **Results:** the module's tests pass on plain and under ASan/UBSan. Under nightly, ASan also checks the 7 compile-fail doctest error codes, which are correct. The new tests pass under Miri.
- **Coverage run:** it ran every suite in the workspace. The only failure is the known `CommitBuilder` doctest.
- **Skipped:** no TSan obligation, BSan not run as you instructed, and no packaging, since the raw bindings didn't change.
- **After landing:** no rebase was needed, because the wave branch was still at `fe6b85bfa`, the tree everything above was measured on. So no gate needed rerunning after landing.

## Dashboard and records
- **Rows filled:** this batch's rows in the five Types tables, their Σ review rows, Coverage stats (total `45.33`% C / `98.85`% Rust), the Overview's Rust line counts, and a Notes entry.
- **Category mapping:** both reports are counted under `+misc`, as earlier reviews counted contracts findings, because the dashboard predates the template's `+contracts` and `+ergonomics` columns.
- **Usage cells:** left to you.
- **Run dir:** it now holds `task.json`, `task.md`, `ffimap.json` and `api-diff.json`.
- **Cleanup:** scratch builds and the temporary base worktree are deleted.

## Evolution
- **Proposed:** `crustify/evolution/ffibox-adoption-of-lifetime-cells`. Ffibox's adoption contract should require the pointee to be a valid value for every lifetime its type names. The same gap affects the crate's 34 hand-written lifetime-carrying types, such as `Reference<'r>`. Ffibox is not mine to change, so it is a proposal only.
- **Not changed:** the open `compile-fail-doctest-codes-unchecked-on-stable` proposal targets the `testing` skill, which my role does evolve. I left it alone, since the task said to judge against the skills as they stand. My nightly ASan run is fresh evidence for it: all 7 error codes check out.
- No skill was changed and no lesson recorded.

Commits carry the campaign identity (Marius Momeu as author, the crustify co-author trailer) and no other trailer, as the `versioning` skill requires.
